Title: Actions, action modifiers and reactions - legality

Messages.Author: Clarendon
Messages.Body:
Is it true you can play reaction and action modifiers at any time during
an action?

ie. A. Bleed
R. Block
AM. +1 stealth
R. Telepathic Counter
AM. Conditioning
R. Telepathic Counter

It's quite important I get an official and accurate answer to this
question as it makes huge differences to the way decks might be
constructed.

Clarendon.

Messages.Author: Brian Wilson
Messages.Body:
Before I could do anything to stop it, Clarendon wrote:

> Is it true you can play reaction and action modifiers at any time during
> an action?

Your minions can use Reaction cards during an action when it is not your
turn. You minions can use action modifier cards during their actions when
it is your turn. This is why Steath enhancers are modifiers and intercept
enhancers are reactions.

You don't have to wait for an "official" ruling on this. Just review your
rules. Note that many reactions and modifiers contain discipline symbols
and text that further limit what actions they can be used with or against.

Clarendon (clar...@crom.demon.co.uk) wrote:
: Is it true you can play reaction and action modifiers at any time during

: It's quite important I get an official and accurate answer to this
: question as it makes huge differences to the way decks might be

Well, Tom is off for a bit (as he posted) so 'official' answers might
have to wait a bit. In the meantime, let me take a stab at it.

It is perfectly legal to play a reaction card in response to either an
action or an action modifier, and it is also equally legal to play an
action modifier in response to any reaction card: thus I would say that
either can be played at any time.

Case in point:

A: Legal Manipulations (total 3 bleed) B: blocks
A: Lost in Crowds (inferior) B: Spirit's Touch
A: Faceless Night B: none
- B lets Bleed through -
A: B: Telepathic Counter (reduced to 2)
B: Telepathic Counter (just drawn,
different minion, reduced to 1)
A: B: Deflection (just drawn)
A: (damn) C: (Grins) Block
(Sports Bike, Raven Spy, shotgun)
A: eeep! Cloak the Gathering C: Cat's Guidance (superior)
A: Bonding (superior) C: :-(
A: phew...

All perfectly legal. Answer your question?

Messages.Body:
dsa...@prism.gatech.edu (Stuart J. Pieloch) wrote:
>
> On an entirely new and as yet unflamed thread
> The concept of playing reactions to an action after not blocking it
> has never actually sunk in on my group
> I.E. After Governing and Conditioning, then play Tele Misd.

I might be wrong of course, but that is how I read it (I think it was
an "official" ruling)

I have to say that I really don't like the idea of you being able to sit
there, not blocking or reacting until the extra bleeds have been put on
and then suddenly producing a Deflection or suchlike. Just doesn't seem
quite right.
>
> We always kinda assumed that you had to block or react then
> Needless to say the Pulsed/Governing/Conditioning bleed that I forced to
> 3 stealth before Tele Misd on my prey for the oust was fun.

I don't like that either, for several reasons. For one, it
makes Malkavian an even more powerful clan (Thank God for Malkavian
Dementias). The second one being that I think if you declare to block then
blocking should be yourreaction. I think it is unbalancing that you can
attempt to block, then when you can no longer match the stealth with your
intercepts, you can just pass it on to your prey. Lets face it, the bleed
is probably quite bigby now (if your predator has been pushing it that
much) and it's got more stealth than even you can intercept, so pity
your prey.

It seems more sensible (and fair) to declare the Deflection or Telepathic
Misdirection immediately on your refusal to block.

This is my opinion; I would like to hear other's. Maybe someone can
persuade me to the contrary.

Clarendon.

So it seems right to you that the offensive player is the only one who
can modify the action after the block is declined? Conditioning / Spying
Mission / Mask of 1000 Faces are all okay, but for some reason Deflection
and Telepathic Misdirection are bogus? Do you let people Telepathic
Counter after declining to block? How about after a Conditioning? Do
you allow Deflection / T. Misdirection after extra stealth is applied to
a bleed?

> >
> > We always kinda assumed that you had to block or react then
> > Needless to say the Pulsed/Governing/Conditioning bleed that I forced to
> > 3 stealth before Tele Misd on my prey for the oust was fun.

> I don't like that either, for several reasons. For one, it makes
> Malkavian an even more powerful clan (Thank God for Malkavian Dementias).
> The second one being that I think if you declare to block then blocking
> should be yourreaction. I think it is unbalancing that you can attempt
> to block, then when you can no longer match the stealth with your
> intercepts, you can just pass it on to your prey. Lets face it, the
> bleed is probably quite bigby now (if your predator has been pushing it
> that much) and it's got more stealth than even you can intercept, so
> pity your prey.

No, you've got this backwards. The way you play makes Malkavian a more
powerful clan. In your scheme, if a predator has _any_ Malkavians then
the prey had better not fail to block or Deflect / Misdirect _anybody_
because once anyone gets through then the (possibly Pulsed) Malkavian will
come in with Mask of 1000 Faces and Condition the bleed and there is
nothing the prey can do. Whereas in normal play, the prey could decline
to block a small bleed and Deflect / Misdirect it should it become a large
bleed.

You are correct that Malkavian is one of the clans that can employ this
defence, but so can Toreador, Tremere, and (to a lesser extent due to no
Auspex) Ventrue. Whereas the only clan to benefit from having no reactions
to bleed mods is Malkavian, since you need both Dominate and Obfuscate.

Perhaps you should try the "standard rules" on this one; it might make
Malkavian Dementia less crucial for your group.

take, whether to reduce the bleed with certainty with one or several T.C's

It's a tricky one and I think the only way I will be convinced one way or

Well, in a way, you can react to modifiers I suppose. After all what are
Intercepts if not reaction cards and reaction modifiers all rolled into
one? :-) I don't have any problem with several reaction cards being
used against an action and action modifiers if the reaction cards all
work along the same lines (such as intercepts), and as long as the reaction
is performed immediately after the initial action.

It very much comes down to what we perceive the cards are actually doing
when we play them in certain situations. I know it's not role playing
but I believe we all tend to get a little into that way of thinking when
we are laying the cards down. The pictures and title on the cards can
influence our perception of what the card can do, more so if you've played
VtMasquerade (ie. The Rotschreck argument).

It's a shame that no-one else who has joined in on this thread has played
the game the "wrong way" as it would have been interesting to also
hear their opinion.

As I said before though, in the long run, it doesn't really matter as
lon as everyone's happy.

Messages.Author: PDB6
Messages.Body:
As for this " I don't block." " Then I Condition you. " issue, we have
always treated it as a sort of " raise/call" response like manuvering in
combat. If someone comes to bleed me, I can try to block, then they can
respond with a modifier, then I can respond and so on. Thus, if both
players pass, the action is called and it occurs. If both players have
declined to respond in order, the action may no longer be modified or
reacted to. For example:

Meth A: I'm coming to bleed you with Ozmo. ( action/raise )
Meth B: I block with Duck. ( reaction/raise )
Meth A: Lost in crowds. +2 stealth. ( reaction/raise )
Meth B: Ok, I'm bled. ( pass )
Meth A: Conditioning. +3 to bleed. ( reaction/raise )
Meth B: Ok then. Marty Deflects you over there. ( reaction/raise )

This works just fine. When Meth B accepted the bleed ( i.e. Passed ),
Meth A could then raise again ( react with a modifier ) or call ( accept
the smaller bleed, with no chance of being deflected. ). Once both
players pass ( play no cards or react in any way ) the action can no
longer be modified in any way. Thus, if Meth B accepts the bleed, and
Meth A passes on modifying it, Meth B cannot then reply by Deflecting it,
because he already passed, and nothing occured that he was allowed to
react to. If you wait to Deflect someone, hoping to draw out their +bleed
before you Deflect them, and they decide not to add that modifier after
they saw you not deflect them, you cannot then Deflect them, as you
already passed, then they called.

This is also how manuvering works in combat. If I, the acting minion,
neglect to manuver to long range ( hoping that you will ), and then you,
the blocking minion, also don't manuver, it's too late for me to go and
manuver to long range.

Once both players pass, it's too late to react or play a card or do
anything. I can play a card, give you a chance to respond, play another,
let you respond again, and then play a third, but if at any time both
players pass ( starting with the blocker ) that's it. The action occurs
as it is.

-Peter D Bakija

I think I missed a chunk of the above thread, so I suspect this was all

I did not mean to compare bleeding to manuvering in game terms, as they
are obviously very different, but in game mechanics terms. Manuvering
works in a " Raise/Pass/Call " system, and this works very well for all
other aspects of the game. Otherwise, alot of the game falls under the
undefined area of " timing " problems, or it becomes a game of " I played
it first. Ha! You loose! " , which is just silly.

-Peter D Bakija
